summary: Kaniksu NF crow's nest site in Boundary County: dated only to the 1930s, listed as abandoned with no date; no source describes what remains.

facts.design: Crow's nest, dated only to the 1930s
facts.status_note: Sources list it as abandoned, with no year given. None says whether the crow's nest still stands.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as Drive-Up

events.note: Crow's nest, dated only as the 1930s; 1930 is the start of that decade, not a year any source gives

evidence.supports: listed under Boundary County as Cedar Ridge
crow's nest dated to the 1930s and abandoned
tagged as a crow's nest with the status abandoned

corrections.why: Every source says abandoned, not destroyed or removed, and none says the crow's nest is gone. firelookout.org marks other lost sites 'Tower Gone' and this one 'Crowsnest Abandoned'.

corrections.proposed: 1930s built (crow's nest); abandoned, no year given
corrections.why: The sources date the crow's nest only to the 1930s and give no year for abandonment.

notes_for_editor: Four thin pages, with no independent corroboration of dates. The Idaho Fire Lookouts page says it has no documented staffing history for this lookout; staffing is left out of the story and facts. The Forest Lookouts page gives only the county, the Kaniksu National Forest and the code 64N-5W-12. Elevation is 5,295 feet on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts, but the facts schema has no elevation key, so it appears only in the story. Coordinates 48.90755, -116.929 match the firelookout.org list. The brief's kind 'platform' is not contradicted, but the sources call it a crow's nest. Search turned up a second Idaho Fire Lookouts URL (north-idaho-panhandle-region/cedar-ridge) that was not read; it probably repeats the same page. A 2011 Boundary County lookouts article (naturallynorthidaho.com) was checked and does not name Cedar Ridge. Do not confuse with Cedar Knob (Idaho County) or Cedar Mountain (Kootenai).
